Which of the graphs above correspond to an invertible function?
worked_solution:
A function is invertible if and only if it's a one-to-one function. To determine which of the functions are one-to-one, we use the horizontal line test.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13932058/assets/cc31f6f291058c7890a9210d5ebfac21cdd961c74c3db5e080d7fca334102b53.png)

From the above, we see that: 

- For graph III, a horizontal line will intersect the curve at most once, no matter where we draw the line. Therefore, graph III shows a one-to-one function. This means that the function is invertible.

- For graphs I, II and IV, some horizontal lines intersect the curve more than once. So, these are not one-to-one functions. As a result, they are not invertible.
